chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ziyad al-Qandy, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'Does the single breast-feeding, the two breast-feedings, and the three breast-feedings make marriage prohibited?' He said, 'No, except what is upon which the bone has strengthened and the flesh has grown.'
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for breast-feeding to make marriage prohibited in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi addresses the juristic debate between the 'number-based' (ta'dadi) and 'substance-based' (ta'siri) schools regarding the validity of breast-feeding (radāʿ) for establishing mahramiyah. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that mere counts of feedings are insufficient; rather, the prohibition is established only when the milk is substantial enough to strengthen the bone and grow the flesh, emphasizing physiological maturity over simple frequency.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ziyad Al Qindy, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘He is Prohibited (from the marriage) from the breast-feeding, and the two breast-feedings, and the three?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, except what the bones are strengthened upon, and the flesh is built’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ziyad al-Qandiy from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
if breastfeeding once or twice brought unlawfulness or three times. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, until it strengthens bones and grows flesh.’”
